Maria: Quick question — we have a safetensors model split into 8 shards but our hotstart only pulls 4/8 initially. How should the loader behave when a shard is missing or fails checksum during warmup?

Dmitri: Manifest-first approach IMO: parse an index/manifest up front, build per-shard metadata (size, checksum, dtype, storage hint) and make a warmup plan. If a shard is missing you have these choices: 1) block until retry, 2) stream-from-origin on demand, 3) swap to a compatible fallback shard (quantized/mmap). Blocking kills latency, streaming increases tail and bandwidth, fallback risks small accuracy diffs.

Carol: +1 for manifest-first. Put an explicit fallback_order array in the manifest so the runtime's behavior is deterministic and auditable, e.g. fallback_order: ["shard-4.quant8.safetensors","shard-4.mmap"].

Hao: Two constraints: S3 object visibility can be temporarily inconsistent (list vs head), so transient "missing" happens. Also streaming partial shard bytes while executing is painful since KV cache wants full tensor slices. We need a clear contract: "can_start_without_all_shards" and what runtime guarantees in that mode.

Maria: Proposal: manifest fields {allow_partial_start: bool, verify_mode: "strict"|"lenient", fallback_order: [urls], tensor_metadata: {dtype, shape}}. Default allow_partial_start=false for safety customers, true for low-latency best-effort.

Evan: If allow_partial_start=true we require a warmup strategy: prioritized shard order (early layers first so forward pass can proceed), and a short stall/placeholder for requests that touch missing slices (e.g., block up to max_block_ms while background fetch proceeds).

Dmitri: WeightSource API should expose per-shard readiness futures and a ReadableSlice abstraction, e.g.:

```
shard = WeightSource.open(shard_url)
await shard.ready(timeout_ms=250)
slice = shard.readable_slice("transformer.wte")
```

Runtime can then await readiness or fallback to an mmap/quant variant. Keep the API small.

Carol: Also include a light verifier: manifest carries a rolling checksum (xxh64) per shard and optional signature. On checksum mismatch consult fallback_order, try next URL. If nothing works: fail hard when verify_mode==strict, else log and continue best-effort.

infra-bot: note: infra currently retries origin reads with exp-backoff up to 8s. Keep that for transient S3 consistency.

Maria: UX: Console should show shard-level statuses (ready / streaming / failed / fallback-in-use) and emit events like "shard-4 checksum mismatch -> used shard-4-quant-v2" for audit.

Evan: Cost/tf tradeoff: storing full quantized fallbacks for every model doubles storage. Suggest lazy-generation of fallbacks on demand and GC after N days unless frequently used. Manifest can point to transient signed URLs created by a build job.

Hao: Edge case: dtype mismatches (fp16 vs int8) mean runtime needs either on-the-fly conversion or an explicit variant mapping in the manifest. Include tensor dtype and layout per shard so the runtime can choose conversion or refuse.

Dmitri: Separation of concerns: manifest proposes fallback candidates, runtime policy picks behavior. Define RuntimePolicy {allow_partial_start, max_block_ms, fallback_strategy: [manifest|stream|fail]}. Keep manifest authoritative about available variants; policy decides enforcement.

Carol: Action items: 1) RFC PR to extend manifest schema (fallback_order, verify_mode, tensor_metadata). 2) Small runtime shim: WeightSource.ready + ReadableSlice + fallback hook. 3) Console events + shard heatmap. I'll open tickets and link.

Maria: Thanks all. I'll draft a short RFC note with manifest examples and runtime pseudocode and ping @eng-runtime for review.

Dmitri: +1

Evan: +1

Maria (follow-up): example manifest snippet: 

```
{
  "model": "foo/1.2.0",
  "shards": [
    {"id":0, "url":"s3://models/foo/0.safetensors", "size":12345, "xxh64":"ab12", "dtype":"f16", "fallback_order":["s3://models/foo/0.quant8.safetensors","s3://models/foo/0.mmap"]},
    {"id":1, "url":"s3://models/foo/1.safetensors", "size":... }
  ],
  "allow_partial_start": true,
  "verify_mode": "lenient"
}
```

Maria: I'll open the RFC and link this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
